sources.entry: Youtarr ⚠ - Download videos from YouTube channels on a schedule via yt-dlp, with a web UI to browse and selectively download videos. Integrates with Plex Media Server and generates NFO metadata for Jellyfin, Kodi, and Emby. ISC Docker

summary.one_liner: Youtarr is a self-hosted, Docker-only YouTube downloader that fetches videos from subscribed channels and playlists on a schedule using yt-dlp, with a web UI and metadata for media servers.
summary.what_it_does: Youtarr automatically downloads videos from subscribed YouTube channels and playlists, with cron-based scheduled runs. Users can pre-validate pasted URLs with a metadata preview, search YouTube from within the app, and browse or selectively download videos through a responsive web UI. It writes NFO files, poster images, and embedded MP4 metadata for media servers, and mirrors subscribed playlists into Plex, Jellyfin, and Emby as native playlists plus a universal .m3u file. It can pull per-video watch status from Plex, Jellyfin, and Emby (one-way, read-only) and includes SponsorBlock segment removal, per-channel quality settings, age/free-space/watched-based auto-cleanup, Apprise notifications, and a REST API with Swagger docs.
use_cases: Automatically archive videos from favorite YouTube channels
Build offline Plex, Jellyfin, Kodi, or Emby libraries from YouTube
Download selected videos from a channel or playlist
Mirror YouTube playlists into media server playlists
Remove sponsor segments from downloaded videos
Set up auto-cleanup of old or watched videos to save disk space
Queue videos from the browser or phone for download
how_to_run: Install Docker, Docker Compose, Git, and a Bash shell (Git Bash on Windows)
Follow the Installation Guide in the documentation for install methods and initial setup
Run ./start.sh for a fresh install (uses Docker named-volume storage for MariaDB)
Alternatively use plain docker compose up -d (may use ./database bind mount)
Open the web UI and complete initial setup and authentication
notable: Watch status sync from Plex, Jellyfin, and Emby covering all users on the server, with filtering by watched state
Channel grouping into subfolders to create separate media server libraries
In-app browser streaming of downloaded videos without a media server
Content ratings normalized to common media-server values like PG-13 and TV-*
Bookmarklet and Apple Shortcuts/Tasker support for queuing videos
caveats: Runs exclusively via Docker; direct npm start or Node deployments are unsupported
Database on virtualized filesystems (Docker Desktop, ARM, NAS) can cause MariaDB migration errors
Intended for personal use; users are responsible for YouTube Terms of Service and copyright compliance
Patreon support is requested for continued development
